risk_if_not_implemented: Without Safety Instrumented Function (SIF), Operational Technology (OT) and embedded systems may fail unsafely or be manipulated, endangering personnel, physical assets and process availability. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), OT Safety / Process Availability Failure (R-OT-1), Injury / Loss of Life (R-SF-1), Physical / Environmental Damage (R-SF-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Utility Service Disruption (MT-7), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control System (ICS) Attack (MT-30).

compensating_control_1.name: Safety Instrumented System (SIS)
compensating_control_1.description: Automated mechanisms exist to monitor and control hazardous processes to reduce the potential negative consequences of hazardous events.
compensating_control_1.justification: Safety Instrumented System (SIS) (EMB-25) provides safety assurance that compensates for the absence of Safety Instrumented Function (SIF) (EMB-26) by providing alternative safety controls that reduce the likelihood and impact of unsafe conditions. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Safe Operations
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to continuously validate autonomous systems that trigger an automatic state change when safe operation is no longer assured.
compensating_control_2.justification: Safe Operations (EMB-23) provides safety assurance that compensates for the absence of Safety Instrumented Function (SIF) (EMB-26) by providing alternative safety controls that reduce the likelihood and impact of unsafe conditions. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
